library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: Suzuki M, Shoji S, Miyoshi S, Krishnaswami S. Model-Based
  Comparison of Dose-Response Profiles of Tofacitinib in Japanese Versus Western
  Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients. *J Clin Pharmacol.* 2020;60(2):198-208.
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.1514>
* Supporting information (Supplementary Tables S1-S4, covariate screening) is
  distributed with the article.

Suzuki 2020 pools the Week 12 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) responses
of two phase 2 dose-ranging studies of tofacitinib monotherapy (placebo or 1, 3,
5, 10 or 15 mg twice daily) in rheumatoid arthritis: a mostly Western study
(NCT00550446) and a Japanese study (NCT00687193). The ACR20, ACR50 and ACR70
responder flags are each fitted with their own Emax model on the logit domain,

$$\mathrm{logit}\,P(\mathrm{ACR}_i = 1) = E_0 + E_{max} \frac{D_i}{D_i + ED_{50}},$$

where $D_i$ is the randomized dose per twice-daily administration (mg). The
final model of each endpoint (Table 4) adds a multiplicative study effect on
$E_{max}$, $E_{max} = E_{max,0}\,\theta_{study}^{x}$ with $x = 1$ for the
Japanese study. The three fits share no parameters, so each is packaged as its
own model file:

| Model file | Endpoint | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `Suzuki_2020_tofacitinib_acr20` | ACR20 at Week 12 | `prob_acr20` |
| `Suzuki_2020_tofacitinib_acr50` | ACR50 at Week 12 | `prob_acr50` |
| `Suzuki_2020_tofacitinib_acr70` | ACR70 at Week 12 | `prob_acr70` |

The dose enters through the covariate column `DOSE_TOFACITINIB_MG` (0 for
placebo) and the study through `STUDY_NCT00687193` (1 = Japanese study,
0 = Western study). There is no PK layer.

```{r load-models}
mods <- list(
  ACR20 = readModelDb("Suzuki_2020_tofacitinib_acr20"),
  ACR50 = readModelDb("Suzuki_2020_tofacitinib_acr50"),
  ACR70 = readModelDb("Suzuki_2020_tofacitinib_acr70")
)
ini_est <- function(fn) {
  d <- rxode2::rxode(fn)$iniDf
  stats::setNames(d$est, d$name)
}
pars <- lapply(mods, ini_est)

# The models have no random effects, so rxode2 warns that a multi-subject
# solve has no omega; only that message is muffled.
solve_typical <- function(m, ev) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev, returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
```

# Population

The analysis set is 648 patients with active rheumatoid arthritis and an
inadequate response to at least one DMARD: 317 from the Japanese study (all
Japanese) and 331 from the Western study after excluding its adalimumab arm
(Table 1). Overall 85.2% were female, mean age 53.4 years (18-83) and mean
weight 62.5 kg (31.4-125; 54.4 kg in the Japanese study and 70.3 kg in the
Western study). Race: 38.7% White, 1.2% Black, 53.7% Asian (all Japanese-study
patients and 31 of the 331 Western-study patients) and 6.3% other. Mean
baseline DAS28-4(ESR) was 6.1 and 6.5 and mean baseline HAQ-DI 1.3 and 1.5 in
the Japanese and Western studies. The same information is stored in the
`population` metadata of each model file.

# Source trace

| Item | Value (ACR20 / ACR50 / ACR70) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Logit Emax model | `logit P = E0 + Emax D / (D + ED50)` | Methods, Base Model Description |
| `D` = dose per administration (mg) | covariate `DOSE_TOFACITINIB_MG` | Methods, Base Model Description |
| Study effect on Emax | `Emax0 * theta^x`, x = 1 Japanese study | Methods, Inclusion of Covariates; Table 2 run 2 |
| ED50 estimated on the log scale | `led50` | Methods, Base Model Description |
| `e0` | -1.3 / -2.3 / -3.2 | Table 4 |
| `emax` (Western study) | 3.2 / 3.7 / 3.2 | Table 4 |
| `led50` | log(4.2) / log(6.1) / log(5.6) mg | Table 4 |
| `e_study_nct00687193_emax` | 1.4 / 1.3 / 1.5 | Table 4 |
| Fraction of maximum placebo-adjusted response | `(p(D) - p(0)) / (p(max) - p(0))` | Methods, Comparison of Dose-Response Profiles |
| Per-study base fits (used for Figure 3 and Table 5 below) | see the next section | Table 3 |
| Placeholder residual `addSd_prob_acr*` | 0.001, fixed | not from source (Bernoulli likelihood) |

# Typical dose-response curves

Replicates the fitted curves of Figure 2 (Japanese only and Western only
panels) of Suzuki 2020.

```{r typical}
dose_grid <- seq(0, 15, by = 0.25)
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(STUDY_NCT00687193 = c(1, 0), DOSE_TOFACITINIB_MG = dose_grid) |>
  mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dv = NA_real_)

solve_ep <- function(ep) {
  out <- solve_typical(mods[[ep]], grid)
  tibble::tibble(
    endpoint = ep,
    study = ifelse(grid$STUDY_NCT00687193 == 1, "Japanese study", "Western study"),
    dose = grid$DOSE_TOFACITINIB_MG,
    p = out[[paste0("prob_", tolower(ep))]]
  )
}
typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mods), solve_ep))

# Closed form of the same parameters: a solve against its own equation, so the
# difference is numerical only.
closed <- typ |>
  mutate(
    e0 = vapply(endpoint, function(e) pars[[e]][["e0"]], numeric(1)),
    emax = vapply(endpoint, function(e) pars[[e]][["emax"]], numeric(1)),
    ed50 = vapply(endpoint, function(e) exp(pars[[e]][["led50"]]), numeric(1)),
    ratio = vapply(endpoint, function(e) pars[[e]][["e_study_nct00687193_emax"]], numeric(1)),
    p_closed = stats::plogis(e0 + emax * ratio^(study == "Japanese study") * dose / (dose + ed50))
  )
stopifnot(max(abs(closed$p - closed$p_closed)) < 1e-8)

ggplot(typ, aes(dose, p, linetype = study)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Tofacitinib dose (mg twice daily)", y = "Probability of response at Week 12",
       linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the fitted curves of Figure 2 of Suzuki 2020 (final model).")
```

At the studied doses the typical probabilities are:

```{r typical-table}
typ |>
  filter(dose %in% c(0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 15)) |>
  mutate(p = 100 * p) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = study, values_from = p) |>
  dplyr::rename("Endpoint" = endpoint, "Dose (mg BID)" = dose) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical responder rates (%) at Week 12, final model.")
```

The curves agree with the fitted lines of Figure 2 read by eye: about 0.21 at
placebo for ACR20 in both studies, rising to about 0.90 (Japanese) and 0.78
(Western) at 15 mg; ACR50 about 0.73 and 0.58 at 15 mg; ACR70 about 0.55 and
0.28 at 15 mg.

```{r typical-fig2}
at15 <- typ |> filter(dose == 15)
at15
fig2_15 <- c(0.90, 0.73, 0.55, 0.78, 0.58, 0.28)
stopifnot(all(abs(at15$p[order(at15$study, at15$endpoint)] - fig2_15) < 0.04))
```

# Simulated trials (Figure 2 prediction intervals)

Suzuki 2020 builds its 90% prediction intervals by simulating the number of
responders per arm from a binomial distribution for 1000 trials. The arm sizes
are not printed; equal allocation of the 317 Japanese and 331 Western patients
over six arms gives 53 and 55 patients per arm.

```{r sim-trials}
set.seed(20200101)
n_arm <- c("Japanese study" = 53L, "Western study" = 55L)
arms <- typ |> filter(dose %in% c(0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 15))
n_trial <- 1000L
sim <- arms |>
  mutate(n = n_arm[study]) |>
  tidyr::uncount(n_trial, .id = "trial") |>
  mutate(rate = stats::rbinom(dplyr::n(), n, p) / n)

pint <- sim |>
  group_by(endpoint, study, dose) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(rate, 0.05), med = median(rate), hi = quantile(rate, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(pint, aes(dose, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(endpoint ~ study) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Tofacitinib dose (mg twice daily)", y = "Responder rate at Week 12",
       caption = "Median and 90% prediction interval of 1000 simulated trials; compare the Japanese-only and Western-only panels of Figure 2.")
```

# Fraction of the maximum placebo-adjusted response (Figure 3, Table 5)

Figure 3 and Table 5 compare where the 5 and 10 mg doses sit on each study's
dose-response curve after removing the difference in Emax,

$$Fr = \frac{p(D) - p(\mathrm{placebo})}{p(\max) - p(\mathrm{placebo})}.$$

Table 5 matches the base model fitted to **each study separately** (Table 3,
"The Japanese Study" and "The Western Study" columns), not the pooled final
model: the final model shares E0 and ED50 across studies and gives different
fractions (shown below for contrast). The per-study fits are not packaged as
model files; they are reproduced here by overriding the `ini()` values of the
packaged models with `STUDY_NCT00687193 = 0`.

```{r fr}
t3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint, ~study,           ~e0,  ~emax, ~ed50,
  "ACR20",   "Japanese study", -1.7, 4.5,   2.8,
  "ACR20",   "Western study",  -1.0, 3.2,   6.2,
  "ACR50",   "Japanese study", -2.6, 5.2,   5.9,
  "ACR50",   "Western study",  -2.1, 3.1,   5.0,
  "ACR70",   "Japanese study", -3.8, 5.0,   4.2,
  "ACR70",   "Western study",  -2.9, 3.0,   7.2
)
fr_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3, time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dv = NA_real_,
  STUDY_NCT00687193 = 0, DOSE_TOFACITINIB_MG = c(0, 5, 10)
)
# Emax at an infinite dose: the drug term tends to Emax.
p_of <- function(ep, e0, emax, ed50) {
  m <- mods[[ep]] |>
    rxode2::ini(e0 = e0, emax = emax, led50 = log(ed50))
  out <- solve_typical(m, fr_ev)
  p <- out[[paste0("prob_", tolower(ep))]]
  pmax <- stats::plogis(e0 + emax)
  (p[2:3] - p[1]) / (pmax - p[1])
}
fr_tab <- t3 |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(fr = list(p_of(endpoint, e0, emax, ed50))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(fr5 = vapply(fr, `[`, numeric(1), 1), fr10 = vapply(fr, `[`, numeric(1), 2)) |>
  select(endpoint, study, fr5, fr10) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(fr5, fr10), names_to = "dose", values_to = "model") |>
  mutate(dose = ifelse(dose == "fr5", "5 mg", "10 mg"))

table5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint, ~dose,   ~study,           ~paper, ~lo,  ~hi,
  "ACR20",   "5 mg",  "Japanese study", 0.78,   0.63, 0.91,
  "ACR20",   "10 mg", "Japanese study", 0.90,   0.78, 1.02,
  "ACR50",   "5 mg",  "Japanese study", 0.43,   0.29, 0.57,
  "ACR50",   "10 mg", "Japanese study", 0.69,   0.55, 0.83,
  "ACR70",   "5 mg",  "Japanese study", 0.32,   0.18, 0.47,
  "ACR70",   "10 mg", "Japanese study", 0.56,   0.40, 0.73,
  "ACR20",   "5 mg",  "Western study",  0.54,   0.31, 0.75,
  "ACR20",   "10 mg", "Western study",  0.73,   0.56, 0.91,
  "ACR50",   "5 mg",  "Western study",  0.41,   0.21, 0.63,
  "ACR50",   "10 mg", "Western study",  0.61,   0.42, 0.82,
  "ACR70",   "5 mg",  "Western study",  0.22,   0.01, 0.46,
  "ACR70",   "10 mg", "Western study",  0.40,   0.17, 0.65
)
```

Table 5 reports the mean and 90% interval of the fraction over 1000 simulated
trials, with the responders at dose D, at placebo and at the maximum effect each
drawn from a binomial distribution. The same simulation with 53 or 55 patients
per arm:

```{r fr-sim}
set.seed(20200102)
fr_sim <- t3 |>
  mutate(n = n_arm[study]) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(sims = list({
    p0 <- stats::plogis(e0)
    pm <- stats::plogis(e0 + emax)
    pd <- stats::plogis(e0 + emax * c(5, 10) / (c(5, 10) + ed50))
    r0 <- stats::rbinom(n_trial, n, p0) / n
    rm <- stats::rbinom(n_trial, n, pm) / n
    f5 <- (stats::rbinom(n_trial, n, pd[1]) / n - r0) / (rm - r0)
    f10 <- (stats::rbinom(n_trial, n, pd[2]) / n - r0) / (rm - r0)
    tibble::tibble(dose = c("5 mg", "10 mg"),
                   sim_mean = c(mean(f5), mean(f10)),
                   sim_lo = c(quantile(f5, 0.05), quantile(f10, 0.05)),
                   sim_hi = c(quantile(f5, 0.95), quantile(f10, 0.95)))
  })) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(endpoint, study, sims) |>
  tidyr::unnest(sims)

fr_cmp <- table5 |>
  left_join(fr_tab, by = c("endpoint", "study", "dose")) |>
  left_join(fr_sim, by = c("endpoint", "study", "dose"))

fr_cmp |>
  transmute(endpoint, study, dose,
            paper = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", paper, lo, hi),
            typical = model,
            simulated = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", sim_mean, sim_lo, sim_hi)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Endpoint" = endpoint, "Study" = study, "Dose (BID)" = dose,
                "Suzuki 2020 Table 5, mean (90% CI)" = paper,
                "Model, typical value" = typical,
                "Model, 1000 simulated trials, mean (90% interval)" = simulated) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Fraction of the maximum placebo-adjusted responder proportion at Week 12, per-study base fits.")

# The typical-value fraction uses the two-significant-figure Table 3 estimates,
# so it rounds to within 0.015 of the printed mean; the simulated mean carries
# Monte Carlo error of about 0.005 on top.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(fr_cmp$model - fr_cmp$paper)) < 0.015,
  max(abs(fr_cmp$sim_mean - fr_cmp$paper)) < 0.04
)
```

The intervals of the simulation are close to the printed 90% CIs (for example
ACR20 Japanese study, 5 mg, printed 0.63-0.91), which supports the assumed arm
sizes.

For contrast, the final (pooled) model gives these typical fractions:

```{r fr-final}
fr_final <- tidyr::expand_grid(endpoint = names(mods), study = c("Japanese study", "Western study")) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    ratio = pars[[endpoint]][["e_study_nct00687193_emax"]]^(study == "Japanese study"),
    e0 = pars[[endpoint]][["e0"]],
    emax = pars[[endpoint]][["emax"]] * ratio,
    ed50 = exp(pars[[endpoint]][["led50"]]),
    `5 mg` = (stats::plogis(e0 + emax * 5 / (5 + ed50)) - stats::plogis(e0)) /
      (stats::plogis(e0 + emax) - stats::plogis(e0)),
    `10 mg` = (stats::plogis(e0 + emax * 10 / (10 + ed50)) - stats::plogis(e0)) /
      (stats::plogis(e0 + emax) - stats::plogis(e0))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(endpoint, study, `5 mg`, `10 mg`)
fr_final |>
  dplyr::rename("Endpoint" = endpoint, "Study" = study) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Fraction of the maximum placebo-adjusted responder proportion, final model (shared E0 and ED50).")
```

# Non-compartmental analysis

Not applicable. The models are landmark dose-response models for a binary
response at Week 12; they carry no drug concentration, so there is no profile
for PKNCA to analyse and the paper reports no NCA.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two-significant-figure estimates.** Table 4 prints E0, Emax, ED50 and the
  study effect to two significant figures; the models use the printed values.
  ED50 is printed on the natural scale and the model stores its logarithm, as
  the paper estimated log ED50.
* **Final model only.** The base models (pooled and per study, Table 3) are not
  packaged. The per-study base fits are used above, through `ini()` overrides,
  to reproduce Table 5 and Figure 3, which the paper derives from them.
* **Three independent fits.** ACR20, ACR50 and ACR70 were fitted separately, so
  the three models do not guarantee `prob_acr20 >= prob_acr50 >= prob_acr70`
  for every covariate value (they do at every studied dose), and a joint
  simulation of the nested responder flags is not defined by the paper.
* **Placeholder residuals.** The source likelihood is Bernoulli with no residual
  error; the fixed additive SD of 0.001 on each probability exists only so the
  model has an observation model.
* **Study, not race.** The retained covariate is the study. All Japanese-study
  patients were Japanese and none of the Western-study patients were, so the
  study effect is also the paper's Japanese/Western contrast; the paper notes
  that the two are confounded. An Asian-race effect (Supplementary Table S1),
  body weight (S2), baseline DAS28-4(ESR) (S3) and baseline HAQ-DI (S4) were
  tested and not retained; no estimates are printed. They are listed under
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Arm sizes.** The per-arm sample sizes of the 1000-trial simulations are not
  printed; equal allocation (53 Japanese and 55 Western patients per arm) is
  assumed.
* **No erratum** was found for the article (Europe PMC search, 2026-11-26).
